metadata.description: C64 Text Adventure Game Soul Crystal

assistant.comment: Pops the caller return address into $41/$42 so the inline descriptor bytes following the JSR can be parsed directly from the caller stream.
Parse the inline descriptor at ($41),Y and store a 16-bit target pointer into $004E/$004F via X=$4E.
Preserve machine state, then tail into the generic vector trampoline at $12F9 using the target loaded into $004E/$004F.

If the first descriptor byte is nonzero, treat the following two bytes as a pointer to a table and copy the first 16-bit entry into the destination at $00,X/$01,X; otherwise copy the next two literal bytes directly.
Saves the BASIC/KERNAL machine state around an indirect dispatch through $004E/$004F, then restores state and resumes through $191B.

Jump indirectly through $004E/$004F. This is a generic engine trampoline, not by itself proof of the main compiled-BASIC P-code dispatcher, because the same vector is reused by the script VM and other engine code.
Fetch the next script token before decoding it.
Tokens below $D0 are expression/operand material; tokens $D0-$EF enter the VM opcode dispatcher.
Copy the current VM PC into an indirect pointer so the next script byte can be fetched.

Read the next operand token, then branch into the variable-class decoders for ranges like $80-$BF.
This value decoder can return 16-bit values from script-visible state slots ($6986-$699B), immediate bytes/words, indexed table lookups, and pointer-indirect fetches. VM opcode E3 relies on that behavior to obtain an indirect callback target in $697C/$697D.
Return the script-visible 16-bit slot at $6990/$6991 as the current decoded value. One possible source for VM opcode E3 indirect callback targets.
Read north_exit_table[index] into the current decoded VM value.
Read east_exit_table[index] into the current decoded VM value.
Read south_exit_table[index] into the current decoded VM value.
Read west_exit_table[index] into the current decoded VM value.
Read up_exit_table[index] into the current decoded VM value.
Read down_exit_table[index] into the current decoded VM value.
Indexed 16-bit lookup from a word table at $6B12 + 2*index. This is another value source that can feed VM opcode E3 with an indirect callback address.
Indexed 16-bit lookup from a word table at $69C6 + 2*index. This can also supply the target address for VM opcode E3 indirect calls.
Store the current decoded 16-bit value into script-visible slot $6986/$6987. Slots like this are valid sources for VM opcode E3 indirect callback targets.
Store the current decoded 16-bit value into script-visible slot $698C/$698D. These script-visible 16-bit slots can later be used as VM opcode E3 callback targets.
Store the current decoded 16-bit value into script-visible slot $6990/$6991. This slot is also used by the text subsystem, but it can equally serve as a VM opcode E3 callback target.
Write object_position_table[index] from the current decoded VM value.
Write object_status_table[index] from the current decoded VM value.
Write visited_room_table[index] from the current decoded VM value.

I scanned the four shipped VM snapshots (disk B1/B2/C1/C2) for real script uses of opcode E3. The only raw 0xE3 bytes in the script region were false positives in disk B2: both occur as the immediate constant form C0 E3 (textoutput = $00E3), not as opcode E3. So this indirect-call opcode appears to be implemented by the engine but unused in the shipped script snapshots.
Uses room_env_flag_group_b/e/d/g plus room_env_flag_group_c/a/h as a composite boolean test; this is likely one of the broader environmental exposure predicates.
Checks the same room_env flag groups for the exact value 1 instead of zero/nonzero, suggesting a narrower room-class predicate over the same current-room metadata.
Another composite test over the room_env flag groups, but with inverted zero logic; this matches its role as the positive 'is exposed zone' predicate seen in the script prologue.
Post-text-display front-end sync: when $695A was set during script_vm_show_text, dispatch svc_frontend_refresh_cycle ($961B) to make the staged output visible.
Dispatch svc_decode_stream ($CB00) with A/X = text/resource id and Y = 0. frontend_io_mode was just forced to $82 for this text output path.
Show-image path finishes by calling svc_frontend_refresh_cycle ($961B), which syncs the staged front-end/screen state after the image/text work.
Lightweight runtime/front-end table maintenance via svc_runtime_swap_tables ($9615). Used as a follow-up helper after image/text-related state changes.
Open the staged front-end work area via svc_frontend_stage_open ($9628) before running the follow-up display/update sequence.
After loading the current room/resource set, dispatch svc_frontend_refresh_cycle ($961B) to synchronize the staged front-end state.
If the current room/resource selector matches the already-loaded state, skip the reload and just dispatch svc_frontend_refresh_cycle ($961B).
After showing the fixed text at $0060, dispatch svc_frontend_refresh_cycle ($961B) so the staged output becomes visible.
Open the staged front-end work area via svc_frontend_stage_open ($9628) before the scripted status/message sequence continues.
Open the staged front-end work area via svc_frontend_stage_open ($9628) for this text/status workflow before continuing with local rendering logic.
Script-visible 16-bit text output / text resource id variable ('textoutput' in the host-side decompiler). Used by showtext() and several SPECIAL flows.
Script-visible 16-bit temporary/result variable ('temp' in the host-side decompiler). SPECIAL($64-$6C) returns boolean results here.
Script-visible 16-bit image id variable ('imageno' in the host-side decompiler). Consumed by the image-display path.
Select VIC bank via CIA2. Low two bits of $94 choose bank $C000-$FFFF.
Set VIC memory pointers. With VIC bank $C000-$FFFF and D018=$F8, screen RAM resolves to $FC00.
Manual decode begins here: LDA $B1D1; LDX $CFF6; optional LSR A; then write filter/resonance to $D417.
Write the current filter/resonance state to SID register $D417.
Load the next volume/filter control byte from $B1D2 and combine it with fade state at $B076-$B078 before writing $D418.
Write the current master volume to SID register $D418.
This entry uses at least one undocumented 6502 opcode (starting with byte $A7), so treat the surrounding raw bytes as real player code rather than plain data.
Confirmed SID init tail: iterate across SID registers at $D400+ and clear them, then clear $D418 and reset player state flag $B077.
Write the prepared SID shadow registers from $B1BA+ to the live SID chip at $D400+, then continue with the main player update.
Loop over the SID register image until all active registers have been written.
Generic helper that parses an inline call descriptor, loads a target vector into $004E/$004F, then dispatches through the shared vector trampoline.

Descriptor-driven resource copy/registration helper.
Parses the same inline descriptor format as $0D4F, then copies a small descriptor record and registers its address window instead of performing the full load path.

Main disk/resource load dispatcher.
Consumes an inline descriptor from the caller, resolves the source pointer/flags, reconstructs optional saved descriptor state, and tail-calls the lower-level transfer helpers through a synthetic stack frame.
Inline descriptor decoder for generic indirect calls.

Generic service-call wrapper for the JMP ($004E) dispatcher.
Before the indirect call, it loads A/X/Y from $030C/$030D/$030E and invokes the selected service entry. This means dispatcher targets should be treated as service routines with a register-based call contract, not as ordinary same-context subroutines.
Shared vector trampoline used by multiple subsystems.

BASIC FAC/value helper entry.
This code manipulates Commodore BASIC floating-point and descriptor workspace around $61-$70, which supports the assessment that part of the binary is tied to a compiled BASIC runtime.

Store a BASIC FAC/value back through an indirect descriptor pointer.
Another strong indicator that this region is compiler/runtime glue built around Commodore BASIC internals.

Main dispatcher for the custom adventure-script VM.
Reads the next token from the script bytecode stream at $6976 and routes it to variable handling, expression decoding, or opcode-specific engine actions.

Advance the script PC and load the next bytecode token.
Uses $6976/$6977 as the VM program counter and stores the fetched token in $6964.

Decode one script operand/value from the bytecode stream.
This is the VM-side reader for constants, variables, and indexed variables used by IF expressions, SELECT CASE, SPECIAL(), and table-driven operations.

Apply the current table-read result to a script variable or indexed variable target.
Used after E4/E5 table fetch opcodes load a value into $699F/$69A0.

Push a return address onto the script VM call stack.
The stack pointer lives at $69A3/$69A4 and stores 16-bit return PCs used by GOSUB/RETURN and SELECT CASE case dispatch.
Pop a return address from the script VM call stack into $69A5/$69A6.

VM opcode E3: call an indirect engine callback.

Decodes one script value into $697C/$697D, copies that 16-bit value into the generic dispatcher vector at $004E/$004F, then invokes call_vector_helper. This is the only dispatcher path that treats the operand itself as a code pointer rather than selecting one of the fixed service entries.
Handler for VM opcode E4: read an 8-bit value from the current script table pointer at $69B3, then apply it to the destination operand.
Handler for VM opcode E5: read a 16-bit value from the current script table pointer at $69B3, then apply it to the destination operand.
Handler for VM opcode E6: load a new table base address into $69B3/$69B4.
Handler for VM opcode E7: return from a script subroutine by popping the VM return stack.
Handler for VM opcode E8: display the text currently selected by the script.
Handler for VM opcode EB: display the image currently selected by the script.
Handler for VM opcode ED: invoke game-specific room/resource selection logic.

Game-specific helper reached from VM opcode ED.
Selects text/resources based on the current room number at $695D and updates the active text pointer in $6990/$6991.
Handler for VM opcode EE: restart/reset via the shared engine entry at $0CDB.

VM opcode EF: SPECIAL(selector) dispatcher.

Selectors below $64 branch to general engine services (load/save/restart, exits, inventory, solution, etc.). Selectors $64-$6C branch to small boolean predicate helpers that return their result in $6992/$6993 (the script-side temp flag).

SPECIAL($66): true when the current command in $6986/$6987 is one of the movement/time-passing commands that should trigger the global exposure/cold checks.

This matches the script prologue, where SPECIAL($66) gates the periodic status-loss logic before room-specific predicates $67-$6A are consulted.

SPECIAL($67): exposed-zone predicate.

Returns true in $6992/$6993 when the current region flag groups indicate one of the 'open/exposed' map areas. Used by all script parts immediately after SPECIAL($66) to decide whether environmental damage logic applies this turn.

General SPECIAL(selector) service dispatcher for selectors below $64.

High-confidence selector map from the shipped scripts:
$01 code-protection/query challenge
$02 load game
$03 save game
$04 restart prompt/flow
$05 endgame/game-over prompt
$06 solution/help flow
$07 music toggle flow
$08 list exits
$09 disk-install / side-swap flow
$0A inventory display
$32 late-game gate/check helper
$33 winning/game-complete flow

Text-display engine entry used by script opcode E8.
Consumes the script-selected text pointer in $6990/$6991 and coordinates message display state.

Dispatch the selected text/resource id through the generic service trampoline.

Copies the current text id from $6990/$6991 into dispatcher_arg_a/x, forces frontend_io_mode=$82, and calls svc_decode_stream ($CB00) through call_vector_helper.
Image-display engine entry used by script opcode EB.

Load the current room/resource set through the generic descriptor loader.
Resets the current stream selector ($6992/$6993), primes room-resource state via $5CDB, then invokes the inline descriptor mechanism through $0CDB.

Load the secondary room/resource set.
Initializes secondary room-resource state via $60DC, selects stream 2 in $6990/$6991, and then dispatches through the same inline descriptor mechanism as the primary loader.

Refresh or switch the compressed-text decode tables before continuing the text-driven front-end flow.

This call site dispatches to svc_prepare_stream_tables ($C903), not to the normal text decode entry.

Refresh current-room state and transient room metadata.

Called after the engine changes $695D/$6D01 or switches movement mode in $6963. It clears transient input/result bytes ($6961/$6962), then populates the per-room working state used by movement helpers and the SPECIAL($64-$6C) environmental predicates. The exact copy path is partly obscured by code Oracle cannot lift cleanly, but the downstream reads show that it feeds the room-environment flag block around $6D18-$6D9F.

Object-description lookup table.
Each 16-bit entry maps an object ID to the text/description resource used when the script reads objectdescription[] (VM token B1).

Per-object points table.
The script VM reads 16-bit entries from here for VM token B0 (points[]).

Object-position table.
Maps each object ID to a room/location ID or special placement code for VM token A6 (objectposition[]).

Object-status table.
Per-object state flags used by VM token A7 (objectstatus[]).

Room-environment flag workspace consumed by SPECIAL($64-$6C).

These bytes behave like the current room's precomputed classification flags. The predicates at $305C, $31AB, and $3317 combine equality/zero tests over this block to decide whether cold/exposure logic should apply. The data appears to be refreshed by refresh_current_room_state ($5396), but Oracle does not yet lift the write path cleanly enough to assign exact meanings to each flag byte.

Direction and room-state tables used by the script VM indexed-variable tokens.

Resolved from the VM read/write helpers:
$6DAA north_exit_table
$6EE2 east_exit_table
$6E12 south_exit_table
$6E7A west_exit_table
$6F4A up_exit_table
$6FB2 down_exit_table
$6C5E object_position_table
$6D04 object_status_table
$7027 visited_room_table
$6B12 points_table (16-bit)
$69C6 object_description_table (16-bit)

South-exit table for the room graph.
Index by room ID to obtain the destination room for south[].

West-exit table for the room graph.
Index by room ID to obtain the destination room for west[].

East-exit table for the room graph.
Index by room ID to obtain the destination room for east[].

Up-exit table for the room graph.
Index by room ID to obtain the destination room for up[].

Down-exit table for the room graph.
Index by room ID to obtain the destination room for down[].

Visited-room flags.
Per-room exploration state used by VM token A8 (visited[]), for example to choose between short and full room descriptions.

Start of the custom adventure-script bytecode stream.
The VM uses $6976/$6977 as its script PC; decompiler sources identify $7600 as the default entry into this tokenized script region.

Parser support table for command NIMM (take).
Reconstruction sources identify this as an object-property/action list used by the adventure parser.

Parser support table for commands SCHLIESSE / OEFFNE (close/open).
Likely triples of object ID plus property/action metadata.
Parser support table for commands VERRIEGELE / ENTRIEGELE (lock/unlock).
Parser support table for command VERRIEGELE (lock).

Parser help/lookup table for command HILF (help).
Entries appear to map object or topic IDs to text/resource IDs.
Parser support table for command ZERSTOERE (destroy).
Parser support table for command SPRICH (talk/speak).

Begin an output/refresh cycle.
If the staged front-end refresh phase has reached 6, the routine forces a full refresh via svc_frontend_refresh_cycle, then advances the phase counter, selects a destination row/vector from $96CB+, flushes the buffered 40-column text to screen RAM, and clears the local buffer.

Append one character to the local 40-column output buffer.
Used by the text/serial decoder path at $CB29 to accumulate output before output_cycle_begin flushes it to screen RAM.

Service contract: lightweight runtime-table maintenance service.
This entry does not consume a meaningful caller payload; it swaps paired runtime tables under banked RAM, performs a small follow-up helper step, and returns.

Dispatcher entry: swap runtime tables, apply one stateful update, then swap back.
This is the heavier sibling of $9615 and appears to perform a one-shot runtime/front-end table update under banked RAM.

Service contract: front-end refresh service.
This entry ignores the incoming register payload for control purposes, preserves A/X/Y across the call, and performs one staged front-end/screen refresh cycle under banked RAM.

Dispatcher entry: clear the local front-end output buffer.
Fills the 40-character buffer at $96EF with spaces and resets the buffered length byte at $96EE.

Service contract: front-end stage-open service.
This entry does not require a meaningful register payload; it runs the first half of the staged front-end helper sequence and returns.

Dispatcher entry: perform the front-end 'stage close' update.
Banks RAM in, runs the second half of the staged refresh helper sequence ($9C67), resets the refresh phase, and clears the visible staging area at $FEF8+.

Save the current C64 memory configuration byte ($01) on a small software stack.
This is used by the runtime and engine when banking BASIC ROM and I/O in and out around ROM-dependent calls.
Restore a previously saved C64 memory configuration byte ($01) from the runtime stack.

Runtime marker/data area associated with the higher-level compiled logic layer.
Contains the literal string "FREE-END", which is a useful signature when separating the compiler/runtime layer from the game-specific script VM.

Music/AV resource setup for the current area or soundtrack selection.
Builds or copies display/music support data into high-memory buffers and triggers follow-up music resource loading via $A92B.

Load a music/display resource sequence from tables near $AA2C.
Walks descriptor tables, copies pattern/control data into display-side buffers, and chains to additional entries when required.

Music/display resource descriptor table used by $A92B.
Entries appear to select source blocks and sequencing information for the soundtrack/display resource loader.

Main VIC/display initialization.
Sets CIA2/VIC bank and screen layout for the game display.
With DD00=$94 (VIC bank $C000-$FFFF) and D018=$F8, the active screen matrix is at $FC00; color RAM remains at $D800.

Swap the active zero-page pointer context with the SID player's saved copy at $B01B-$B028.
This lets the music engine borrow $E0-$ED as work pointers without permanently clobbering the caller's state.

Wait for SID fade-out completion.
On first entry, seeds the fade state ($B076/$B078/$B077), then busy-waits until bit 6 of $B077 is set by the output tail after the volume ramp reaches zero.

SID filter/master-volume output tail.
Applies the current filter/resonance byte from $B1D1 to $D417, then combines $B1D2 with the fade state in $B076-$B078 before writing the final master-volume value to $D418.

SID filter/volume update tail.
Updates SID filter control at $D417 and master volume at $D418 from player state around $B076-$B078 and $B1D1/$B1D2.

Recovered SID player init/reset entry (partially manual).
This block appears to use undocumented 6502 opcodes during state setup, which prevents full automatic lifting. The confirmed tail clears SID registers at $D400+ and zeros $D418 / $B077 before returning.

Main SID player tick entry.
Swaps in the player zero-page pointer set, runs one sequencer frame at $B33D, then restores the previous zero-page context before returning.

Main 3-voice SID sequencer/update routine.
Advances per-voice pattern/instrument state, updates the shadow SID register block at $B1BA+, and finishes by flushing those registers to $D400-$D416 before the filter/volume tail runs.

SID register flush/output step.
Copies a prepared register image from player state tables at $B1BA+ into the live SID register block at $D400+.

Pointer to the active SID song header.
Init code at $B2E0 loads this word into $E0/$E1, then reads offset +6 as the song speed/divider byte and uses offsets +0/+2/+4 as the three voice sequence pointers.

Pointer table for SID phrase/event streams.
The player doubles the sequence byte and indexes this table to reach phrase data blocks such as $BA13, $BA19, $BA72, $BA8D, $BAAB, $BAC7, $BB50, and $BB74.

Embedded SID song header.
This header provides three per-voice sequence/order-list pointers ($BA02, $BA07, $BA0A) plus the frame divider/speed byte at $BA00.

Prepare or switch decode tables for the compressed stream layer.
This wrapper selects which table set to use based on the current stream selector and cached values in $CFF2/$CFF3, then loads the corresponding record through svc_write_block / bulk table helpers before restoring memory configuration.

Service contract: compressed-stream/text service.
Inputs arrive in A/X/Y via dispatcher_arg_a/x/y. In the common text path from $4022, A/X/Y carry the selected text/resource id as a 24-bit tuple with Y usually zero; when Y==2, the service first refreshes stream tables before decoding.

Send a 3-byte command header over the custom DD00 serial protocol.
A carries the command id; X/Y are forwarded as parameters. The routine computes several DD00 line masks in $CF9B-$CF9F, temporarily switches the bus to transmit mode, sends A/X/Y with serial_write_encoded_byte, then restores the previous DD00 state.

Read one 84-byte block from the custom DD00 serial protocol into the buffer pointer at $AD/$AE.
Uses serial_expect_zero_byte as a framing check and serial_read_block_84_bytes as the inner transfer loop.

Top-level compressed stream decode entry.
Optionally refreshes/loads decode tables through $C900 when Y==2, then decodes one table-selected stream record and either expands Huffman-like text through $CEF2 or follows an alternate rendering path. Output characters are emitted through stream_emit_char_with_wrap at $CB29.

Main Huffman-like text decode loop.
Initializes the decoded-length counter from two bytes read over the serial transport, then walks a binary code tree using $CA00/$CA80 as the two branch tables. Terminal symbols have bit 7 set; after masking with $7F the decoded character is emitted via stream_emit_char_with_wrap.

SID base address.
The actual music player updates the live sound chip registers here; higher-level soundtrack selection happens in the engine code around $A77A-$AA2C.
Probable music/pitch or instrument data table in the banked SID data area.
Probable compact music control/instrument table referenced by the music loader at $A92B/$AE00.

Color RAM for the visible character screen.
Used together with the screen matrix at $FC00; color RAM is fixed at $D800 on the C64.

Display buffer area inside the active VIC bank.
Runtime code writes screen-related data here while the display bank is $C000-$FFFF; this sits near the active screen matrix at $FC00.

Active screen matrix (screen RAM) for the main game display.
Derived from the display setup DD00=$94 and D018=$F8 in the VIC initialization at $AED2.
